comment: Many countries implementing DPI-H operate in multilingual contexts, and health workers may use languages at the point of service that differ from those used to author national terminology, value sets and data-collection forms. Localisation therefore extends beyond language to include conventions for dates, numbers and currencies in shared content.

public.text: Many countries implementing DPI-H operate in multilingual contexts, and health workers may use languages at the point of service that differ from those used to author national terminology, value sets and data-collection forms. Localisation therefore extends beyond language to include conventions for dates, numbers and currencies in shared content.
public.suggestedRevision: Consider expanding the Terminology Service articulation in §3.5.3.1 and Appendix C to explicitly address multilingual and localisation requirements, including the ability to associate multiple language designations with concepts and provide translated display terms for value sets
